source: Dawson-Glass et al. Ecology 2025 doi:10.1002/ecy.4504 Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.sbcc2frh4

guild_mapping.source_field_caveat: Dryad species_info.csv Functional field not directly read; mapping externally confirmed with botanical Poaceae genera

method.guild_normalization: Each guild closed to its own pot guild-biomass total

placebo.conditioned_rule: Bromus and Dactylis assigned to grass, Rumex assigned to forbs
placebo.interpretation: Partition-rank diagnostics, not a randomized treatment p-value; grouping post hoc

interpretation: Whole-community unlabeled ranks weak, broadleaf-guild unlabeled rank highly history-associated; strong forb guild shift primarily Rumex; without Rumex, among 9 forbs, labeled identities retain history but their unlabeled ranks do not. Signals are not additive across differently normalized representations.
limitations: The original paper already showed effects of germination timing and species-specific biomass; new claims are descriptive nested decomposition only.
Post hoc analysis of same 24 mesocosms; no new independent biological replication.
No inference of competition mechanism or ecosystem function from group biomass shares.
No direct reading of source species-info Functional column; botanical guild classification externally verified.
Forb guild mapping unusually high among 3003 partitions but ordinary among 220 anchored partitions; do not claim unique guild mechanism.
p>.05 is not proof of no effect; E is not Shannon/mutual information.
Main KNK manuscript frozen v28-v38 unchanged; new validation PR stays draft.

loo_posthoc_descriptive.model: fixed-penalty L2 logistic (lambda=4), each whole pot held out once, fold-local scaling
loo_posthoc_descriptive.warning: Subgroup was selected after inspecting this same dataset. Not an independent external performance estimate, no formal p value.
